_comment: All lengths are in INCHES. Source: Sleeves & Openings Standards Manual. Edit family names/params to match your library.
_familiesComment: Office (MPI) families, Revit 2026, category Mechanical Equipment. A null *Param is detected from the loaded family (Width/Length/Diameter/Comments and common variants); set it explicitly if detection picks the wrong one. Verify in Setup > Map Families.

roundSleeve._sizeTogglesComment: This family has no diameter parameter: each size is a Yes/No parameter '<prefix> <size>' (Storm 4..12, Sanitary 4..12, Vent 4..12, Fire 3..10, Gas 3..10, Cold Water 2..12, Hot Water 3..4, Electrical 2..5, Condensate 3). The add-in ticks the one for the system + size and unticks the rest; a size the family lacks rounds UP to the next available. TO CONFIRM WITH OFFICE: DryerExhaust -> Vent? Bathtub -> Sanitary (or the Double Sleeve for Tub family)? Sizes are sleeve sizes, not pipe sizes?

naming._damperPattern: Auto Run: a damper the riser diagram draws on a duct (MD, FSD, GD) is written on that duct's opening, e.g. ERV-SA-FSD. {damper} = the damper code(s).

exhaust._firstNumberEastWest: Auto Run: true = the first number of a duct size (16X8 -> 16) always runs east-west (Revit X), as labelled on the plan (office rule, 2026-09-27). false = turn the opening the way the engineer drew the duct (outline or riser block shape).

dryerExhaust._shaftOpening: Auto Run: dryer ducts drawn closer than minSpacing (a dryer shaft) get one Regular Opening around them all, 2" clear each side, named DE (rule 74, as the office sets draw it). Roof shafts stay for review (rule 78: 6"x6" per duct). false = every dryer shaft goes to review.

clearances._ervFloorComment: Auto Run: the ERV supply and exhaust openings on a floor are grouped this far apart, centre to centre (rule 54; the office's S&O sets draw them 12" c-c). On the roof they are ervSpacingExact apart, edge to edge (rule 55).
clearances._linkedComment: Columns, beams and walls are also read from linked Revit models (the structural model is usually a link). linkedModelMatch = regex on the link name, empty = all links.

levelClassification._comment: Regex (case-insensitive) matched against level names, tried in the order ignore, bulkhead, roof, setback, cellar; first match wins; unmatched levels are apartment floors. JSON needs \b for a regex word boundary. Ignore = reference levels (top of steel / slab, parapet): never a floor, nothing is placed or propagated there. Override any level in Project Setup.

generalRules._comment: Confirmed at the start of Project Setup and before any work (manual p.2). A No blocks the add-in.
mustConfirm: I am working from the Owner's plan, not the Approved plan.
I checked and confirmed this file is the latest version.

fixtures._comment: Manual p.2 'Always verify': the add-in finds these fixtures in the model (family/type/category name matched case-insensitively) and checks the sleeves against them in Final Check. Lengths in inches.

legend._comment: Auto Run: tag meanings are read from the engineer's PDF (ABBREVIATIONS table, SYMBOLS list, schedules). officeFixed = tags the office always uses and PDFs do not define (only KX and TX). categories are tried in order against the definition text (regex, case-insensitive); the first match wins. system = gets an opening of that system; ignore = no opening; labelOnHost = no opening, but the tag is added to the label of the duct opening it sits on (ERV-FSD). review = not decided yet: reported with that text, not placed. For the note written next to an untagged riser: shaft = the ducts drawn there go up in a shaft and get one opening around them all (2" clear each side, roof +4"), named this, on every slab the shaft passes; system + label = that riser is an opening of this name, its round size read from the note (8Ø) or diameter; check = placed but flagged with this text. A definition matching nothing is 'not a riser'. Also applied to the note written next to a riser that has no tag.

categories.label: GMV
categories.check: gas vent: confirm the gas scope with the engineer before cutting (the plumbing set may say the water heaters are electric)
gas vent: confirm the gas scope with the engineer before cutting (the plumbing set may say the water heaters are electric)

dwgProfile._comment: Auto Run: how the engineer draws risers in the DWG. riserBlocks = regex on the block (or dynamic-block source) name drawn at a riser's centre; tagBlocks = regex on the tag bubble block; tagAttributes = bubble attributes joined into the riser name (TX + 1 = TX1, ERV + SA = ERV-SA); connectorLayers = regex on layers of the line from bubble to riser. Distances in inches. Defaults match 24 Skillman (Precision Engineering Group).
dwgProfile._leaderTextDistance: A classic LEADER (not a multileader) that is not linked to its text reads the text nearest its tail, up to this far (inches).
dwgProfile._ductLayers: Regex on layers holding the duct outlines (rectangles / the X in a riser): a rectangular opening is turned the way its duct is drawn.
dwgProfile._sectionMark: A riser drawn on a duct layer as a section mark (rectangle or circle crossed by a diagonal) is its own riser, even beside a shaft of riser symbols (TX1 next to the dryer ducts). Marks outside sectionMarkMinSize..sectionMarkMaxSize (inches) are ignored; a riser symbol within outlineTolerance of a mark is the same duct.
dwgProfile._referenceFolders: Regex on folder names (searched next to the model) holding the per-floor drawings at Revit's 0,0 (office xrefs). Used to line the DWG up with Revit for floors that have no DWG imported/linked in the model.
dwgProfile._gridFiles: Regex on the file name of the office grid-lines DWG (same 0,0 as the xrefs), searched in and next to the xref folder. Its grids must land on the Revit grids (this model's, or a Revit link's) within 1", or nothing is placed.

sleeveViews._comment: Auto Run: after placing, one plan per floor that has sleeves/openings, as in the PL model: a copy of that level's plan (mechanical first) named '<level name><nameSuffix>', Sub-Discipline = subDiscipline (the Project Browser folder), the manual's view range (unless a view template sets it), every opening tagged when a tag family for its category is loaded. An existing view with that name is reused.
sleeveViews._tag: false = no separate tags: the opening shows its riser name itself (Openings family: 'Riser Number' in its corner). Tags Auto Run placed earlier in the Sleeves views are removed. true = tag every opening with the category's default tag.
sleeveViews._transparentLabels: true = the name text drawn inside the opening families (Riser Number) gets a transparent background: the family's text types are set to Transparent and the family is reloaded (instance values kept).

automation._comment: Auto Run after placing and the checks against other sets. finalCheck = run Final Check on the openings this run placed; autoFix = apply its fixes that have one right answer (size, name, riser id) to those openings only (never moves, copies or deletes). riserDiagram = read the engineer's riser diagram and report tagged risers (GX-1...) the floor plans do not show. referenceSet = TESTING ONLY (enabled: false in normal use; the S&O set is what Auto Run produces): a finished Sleeves & Openings set (PDF) of a past project to compare with: files = regex on PDF names searched in the project folder; its HVAC openings are the rectangles in the colour of the legend row legendText; tags = text up to maxTagSize points inside them; each sheet is lined up by its grid bubbles (all within gridTolerance). Openings within matchRadius are paired, then compared: position within positionTolerance, size within sizeTolerance. Inches.

decisions._comment: Cases the manual or the engineer's notes settle, decided by rule instead of left for review. trustUpFromBelow = a crossing only the floor below shows, labelled UP there, is placed straight above it (manual 23, 45-51). dryersIntoHost = dryer ducts landing on another opening make that opening bigger to take them (rule 74). roofDryerGrid = roof dryer shafts get a 6x6 per duct in straight rows of roofDryerPerRow, dryerExhaust.minSpacing clear between them (rules 78-82). mergeOverlaps = openings on one slab that overlap become one opening around both, named with both tags (manual 21). avoidStructure = an opening in a beam or shear wall (rules 27-28), within 1'-0" of a column (rule 26) or on a wall edge is first reshaped to the same duct area up to maxAspect:1 (engineer's general note: duct dimensions can be reconfigured up to 4:1 keeping the area), then moved up to maxShift in shiftStep steps; skipped only when neither clears it. Inches.

pdfOnly._comment: Auto Run with the PDF only (plumbing model, DWG field left empty). The PDF must be a vector plot from CAD that keeps its layers: pipe circles, leaders and tag bubbles are read by layer as in the DWG (plumbing.dwgProfile), the service text next to each bubble, and the columns of the architectural background (columnLayers, rectangles columnMinSize..columnMaxSize). Each floor page is lined up with Revit by matching its columns to the model's columns (host and loaded links): at least minColumns within columnTolerance, spread minSpread feet each way, fitting the printed scale within scaleTolerance, and clearly better than any other placement. A page with too few columns follows the floor next to it when minStacked pipes land within stackTolerance. The tag numbers inside the bubbles are strokes, not text: stacks are numbered 1, 2, 3... (same number on every floor). placeWhenPassed = false sends every PDF-only sleeve to review. Inches unless noted.

soSheets._comment: The S&O set (SO_SHEETS_PLAN.md): one sheet per floor that has a '<level> Sleeves' view, built like the pattern sheet (patternSheet, or the lowest numberPrefix sheet holding a Sleeves view: SL101 on 24 Skillman): its title block and switches, the plan at the same spot, the legend, a copy of its schedule with the Level filter set to the floor, the floor label (text of type floorLabelType in the plan, rewritten) and texts of copyTextTypes. Names: {Floor} = '1st Floor' / 'Roof', {FLOOR} = upper case, {index} = the sheet's place in the set (1st... '8th' for the 24 Skillman roof), {kind} = floor / roof / bulkhead / cellar. Existing sheets are only completed, never rebuilt or deleted. Notes = revisions in the title block's revision table (NOTES TO ARCH, ENG, & G.C.), marked with notesTag in Issued By; the office's own revisions are never touched. afterAutoRun / pdfAfterAutoRun: done at the end of Auto Run in the PL / FP model. PDF: pdfName in the folder named pdfFolder found next to the model or the drawings Auto Run read (24 Skillman: Project Files/Structural); {project} = the model name with projectNameStrip removed.

modelKind._comment: Which kind of model Auto Run is in (HV runs mechanical; PL and FP run plumbing and sprinkler). In order: the answer the user saved in the model (asked only when nothing else decides, or when the drawings disagree with the model); the file name (plumbing.modelMatch, sprinkler.modelMatch, hvMatch; '_' counts as a separator); what the model holds, not its links (ducts + air terminals + hydronic pipes vs plumbing pipes + plumbing fixtures + fire pipes + sprinkler heads, pipes by their system type): decides when the larger side has at least minElements and ratio times the other; then other signs (plan view disciplines, worksets, sheet numbers, sleeves already placed). If none decides, the drawings' sheet numbers do (M-, P-, SP-), and if they do not either the user is asked once.

plumbing._comment: Auto Run in the PL model (model name matching modelMatch). The plumbing engineer draws every pipe through a slab as a small circle on its system's layer, groups them in a chase with a tag bubble (P1, P2...) joined by a leader, and writes the services next to the bubble, one per line: 'S UP & DN', 'V RISE & DN', 'ST DN', 'V THRU ROOF'. UP = the slab above, DN / THRU = this floor's slab. Each sleeved service becomes a round MPI sleeve named '{service}-{riser}' (S-P3), pipe + sleeveOverPipe rounded up to the next of sleeveSizes (storm/standpipe rule: pipe + 2"). Plans carry no pipe sizes: services.*.pipe is used and the row says so. The pipes of a group are drawn 5" apart: their sleeves are set in a row sleeveGap apart. Lowest level = slab on grade: no sleeves (skipLowestSlab). Fixture labels (WC, LAV, BT...) use fixtureSleeves 'model': the nearby matching Revit fixture's sanitary connector is used; ambiguous or connector-less fixtures remain review. Water is not sleeved (the office S&O sets show sanitary, vent, storm and gas only). Inches.

sprinkler._comment: Auto Run for sprinkler / standpipe sleeves. The office has no FP model: Auto Run in the PL model asks 'Plumbing' or 'Sprinkler / standpipe' (enabled = false hides the question); a model matching modelMatch goes straight to sprinkler. Same pipeline as plumbing, but the fire protection engineer labels each pipe in words with its size and a leader to its riser symbol: '3" SPRINKLER RISER UP/DN', '2" SPRINKLER CHUTE RISER UP/DN', '4" FDC DN'. services.*.match = regex on that label; the size in the label is the pipe size (services.*.pipe only when none is written). UP = the slab above, DN = this floor's slab; a label with neither (the roof's '3" SPRINKLER RISER W/ INSPECTOR TEST TEE') = the pipe ends on this floor (unmarked = DN), placed only when the floor below sends it up, else review. Sleeve = pipe + sleeveOverPipe rounded up to sleeveSizes (manual: standpipe = pipe + 2"), MPI sleeve 'Fire' toggle. Chute risers run inside the garbage chute opening: no sleeve, listed. Lined up by the per-floor Xref SPR drawings (referenceFolders), checked on the risers labelled there. PDF only (leave the DWG empty): the same labels and leaders read from the vector PDF, lined up by the columns as for plumbing (rules.json pdfOnly). Inches.

dwgProfile._connectorLayers: PDF only: the layers the leaders are drawn on (a line with a filled arrowhead). The DWG route reads every LEADER entity whatever its layer.

CHUTE.note: sprinkler riser inside the trash chute: it goes through the chute opening, no sleeve

adopt._comment: Setup > Adopt Existing: stamps openings/sleeves that were placed by hand so Final Check, Riser Manager, Propagate and Schedule see them. All regexes are case-insensitive. System is decided in this order: 1. nameToSystem on the label (nameParams) and on the type name; 2. for checkbox-sized sleeves, the prefix of the toggle that is ON via togglePrefixToSystem; 3. the matcher's default system. Systems the manual sizes (Exhaust, GarbageChute, DryerExhaust, MotorizedDamper, Refrigeration, Electrical, Storm, AreaDrain, Condensate, Standpipe, Bathtub, Toilet, ERV) get size checks; any other name (Sanitary, Vent, ColdWater, HotWater, Gas...) is still checked for structure, wall edges, overlaps and riser continuity.
